items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I worked with him the last two years of his life and I always found him a great guy.

ctx.x: Okay. So you didn’t have a family that disallowed blues in the house?

Oh no. No it was a very secular thing. We knew those people but, in fact I even divided it up even more than that. The people who don’t listen to the blues because it’s the devil’s music or something like that, still have a body of secular music that, that’s part of their life too. You know you could say it’s folksy or something like that. But you know when you hear people like King Curtis or “Fathead” Newman, that is David Newman, (we don’t want to call him “Fathead” on this) — I worked with him the last two…
Yeah. He spent some good years with Ray Charles.
